name: economy
author: LLM, from a scenario. NOT hand-tuned numbers — a statement of what good means.
scenario: A space trading economy where progression feels EARNED. The player should hunt for profitable routes and feel clever finding them — but no single route may trivialise the game, and no route may pay forever. Money should come from working the whole map across several commodities, not from one wiki-known loop. Affording the next ship should take a few sessions, not a few minutes.

constraints.why: THE GATE. A route must EXHAUST ITSELF as you work it. If the best route still pays the same at hour 60 as at hour 1, it is a riskless unbounded money printer and the whole progression is a formality. Note what this asks: it cannot be satisfied by ANY choice of prices, because with static prices the decay is exactly zero by construction. If the optimiser satisfies this, it did so STRUCTURALLY.
a few sessions of play. Under 6h the ship ladder is meaningless; over 25h it is a grind.
if one route earns most of the money, the map collapses into a single loop and the other stations are scenery.
more than one thing must be worth carrying, or the cargo hold is a formality.
the whole map should be worth visiting.
an income that neither starves the player nor floods them.
